purpose: Click is a Python library for building command-line interfaces. It is composable: commands, groups, options and arguments are built from decorators or classes. It handles parsing, help generation, prompts, shell completion and testing.
intended_users: Python developers writing CLI applications. Maintainers and contributors working on Pallets/Click itself.
dependencies: Runtime: no dependencies are declared in pyproject.toml. The [project] table has no dependencies key. I did not check for a Windows-only dependency such as colorama.
docs group: sphinx, myst-parser, pallets-sphinx-themes, sphinx-tabs, sphinxcontrib-log-cabinet

entry_points.description: Command.main() runs a CLI: it reads args, handles shell completion, builds the context, invokes the command and maps exceptions to exit codes. Command.__call__ is an alias for it (line 1651).
The public API surface: it re-exports names from core, decorators, exceptions, formatting, globals, termui, types and utils.
CliRunner, the public testing entry point. Its contents were not read; tests use it via the `runner` fixture.

key_modules.role: Context, Command, Group, CommandCollection, Parameter, Option and Argument, plus ParameterSource. It holds main(), make_context, parse_args, invoke, resolve_command and the parameter value pipeline (consume_value, type_cast_value, process_value, handle_parse_result).
key_modules.feature_relevance: Most new behaviour goes here: new Option/Argument/Command/Group parameters, value handling, help specs, and the info dict (to_info_dict).

key_modules.role: Decorators: command, group, option, argument, pass_context, pass_obj, make_pass_decorator, version_option, help_option, confirmation_option, password_option, custom_version_option.
key_modules.feature_relevance: A new core parameter usually needs a matching decorator keyword or a new decorator. Typing tests exercise these.

key_modules.role: ParamType and its implementations: Choice, File, Path, IntRange, FloatRange, DateTime, UUID, Tuple, BOOL, INT, FLOAT, STRING and UNPROCESSED, plus the convert_type function.
key_modules.feature_relevance: Add new parameter types or change conversion.

key_modules.role: Internal option parser, now private as _OptionParser, _Option, _Argument and _ParsingState. The old public names go through deprecation shims.
key_modules.feature_relevance: Changes to how option tokens are parsed.

key_modules.role: Interactive and terminal helpers: prompt, confirm, style, secho, progressbar, edit, launch, pause, getchar, echo_via_pager and clear. The implementation is in _termui_impl.py.
key_modules.feature_relevance: Add or modify terminal UI features.

key_modules.role: Shell completion: CompletionItem, shell_complete and split_arg_string. Command.main calls it when the _PROG_COMPLETE environment variable is set.
HelpFormatter and wrap_text, used for help output.

ClickException hierarchy: UsageError, BadParameter, MissingParameter, NoSuchOption, NoSuchCommand, BadArgumentUsage, BadOptionUsage, FileError, Abort, plus Exit (used in core.py but not re-exported in __init__.py).
key_modules.feature_relevance: New error types or error message changes.

key_modules.role: echo, open_file, format_filename, get_app_dir, and private helpers such as _LazyFile and _KeepOpenFile. Several old public names are now deprecated aliases.
CliRunner for invoking commands in tests.
key_modules.feature_relevance: Test-support features. Its contents were not read.

key_modules.role: Platform and stream compatibility helpers. Not read.
get_current_context and the context stack. Not read.

execution_flow: Command.main (core.py:1483) takes args from sys.argv[1:], expanding globs on Windows via _expand_args, or from the args you pass. It detects the program name and calls _main_shell_completion (line 1619). If the _<PROG>_COMPLETE env var is set, that function runs shell_complete and exits. Otherwise main opens `with self.make_context(prog_name, args, **extra) as ctx` and calls self.invoke(ctx). make_context calls parse_args. For each parameter, parse_args calls Parameter.handle_parse_result (core.py:2763), which does the following: consume_value picks a value and a ParameterSource; a deprecation warning is echoed to stderr if the value was set explicitly; process_value runs type conversion and callbacks; then the value is stored in ctx.params, with arbitration when several parameters share one name. Group.invoke dispatches to subcommands through resolve_command (core.py:2088). In standalone mode main then calls ctx.exit(). Exit, Abort, KeyboardInterrupt/EOFError, ClickException and EPIPE OSError are caught and turned into exit codes and messages. With standalone_mode=False, the return value is returned and exceptions propagate.
test_runner: pytest. pyproject.toml sets testpaths=tests and filterwarnings=error. addopts is `-m 'not stress'`. tox runs it across Python 3.10–3.14 plus 3.14t and pypy3.11 (both listed in the tox env_list).
test_conventions: tests/conftest.py provides a function-scoped `runner` fixture that returns CliRunner().
Plain pytest functions with bare asserts. Parametrization is used heavily, for example `ids=lambda ...` in test_deprecations.py.
Warnings are errors (filterwarnings=error), so a test that triggers a warning on purpose must wrap it in pytest.warns(...). For example, `pytest.warns(DeprecationWarning, match=name)`.
Test files are grouped by source module. Subpackages tests/test_types/, tests/test_utils/ and tests/test_exceptions/ hold one file per class or function, named test_<Name>.py.
tests/typing/*.py are example files checked by mypy and pyright (the `typing` tox env). They are not run by pytest.
Stress tests carry `@pytest.mark.stress` and are excluded by default.

compatibility_rules.claim: Supported Python is >=3.10, and the package is typed (Typing :: Typed classifier, py.typed file in src/click).

The public API is whatever src/click/__init__.py re-exports using the `X as X` form. Names beginning with an underscore are private. Old names are kept as lazy module `__getattr__` shims that emit DeprecationWarning.

Deprecation practice: the message says 'is deprecated and will be removed in Click 9.0' (or 9.1 for __version__), uses DeprecationWarning with stacklevel=2, and names the replacement. The old name still resolves to the private implementation.
core.py also has a module-level __getattr__ shim for BaseCommand and MultiCommand.
Each deprecated alias must have a test in test_deprecations.py (parametrized case plus an AttributeError check for unknown names).
Warning policy: pytest runs with filterwarnings=error, and the docs build uses -W.
Typing policy: mypy runs in strict mode over src and tests/typing, and pyright runs with --verifytypes click.
The code uses `from __future__ import annotations`. ruff enforces isort with force-single-line imports and the `typing as t` alias.
Changes are recorded in CHANGES.md using {pr}/{issue} roles. Docstrings use `.. versionchanged::` / `.. versionadded::` directives.
User-facing strings go through the gettext `_()` function. The deprecated-parameter message in handle_parse_result is one example.

setup_and_test_commands.purpose: Install the default dependency groups (dev, pre-commit, tests, typing). The command itself is not in the file; it is inferred from [tool.uv] default-groups.
Run the tests (testpaths=tests; stress tests are excluded).
Run the full matrix: Python 3.10–3.14, 3.14t, pypy3.11, style, typing, docs and the stress environments.
Run the stress tests only (`pytest -m stress`).
